criterionFindings.replayExpiryEnforcement: PASS. Claim store requires BOTH eventId and nonce unseen before claiming (MemoryPublishedTaskPersistence.claimReplay; SQL PublishedReleaseStore.claimReplay selects WHERE event_id OR nonce). Fresh claim required; identical replay of an already-published packet returns outcome 'duplicate' by payloadHash+manifestHash identity, and one publication is stored (portable 9/9 and durable-live duplicate:true with boardEntries:1, claimRows:1). Divergent content is rejected with exact codes: same eventId/new nonce/different bytes => 'replay' (both portable and durable-live); fresh eventId/nonce with content drifting from an already-published (taskId,version) => 'task_conflict' (security test 10 and durable-live conflict:true). Expiry: expiresAt <= now => 'expired' WITHOUT touching the claim store (security test asserts claims stay empty); window above the 15-minute maximum (expiresAt - now > 900000 ms) => 'invalid_envelope'; private side bounds ttlSeconds to [15,900] with 300 s default while the DDL/reader caps the package at 134217728 bytes. Contrived beyond-window behaviour is honestly disclosed: an identical replay arriving after expiry is treated as 'expired' rather than 'duplicate' since publication persistence is idempotent and store rows are immutable — consistent with the receiver's expiry-first ordering.
